messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: scatterplots with time
parts:
I think that in shinystan it would be good to plot the scatterplot between 2 variables with light lines connecting the dots so that it gives some sense of the trace as well as of the joint distribution of the simulation.

> On Mar 2, 2015, at 8:46 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>
> I agree that's what it looks like. Looks like your
> message cut out. What do the other parameters look like?
> A pairs() plot may help you see what's going on --- often
> two parameters will both jump together.
>
> Having more parameters than data points isn't necessarily
> an issue if you have priors that weakly identify the model.
>
> - Bob
>

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] scatterplots with time
parts:
If you have 2000 draws and plot lines like this, you'll
get a giant hairball. But for 50 draws it might be
readable.

The lines I'd like to see would correspond to posterior means
and/or estimated density countours. It's often hard to see the posterior
mean among the samples.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] scatterplots with time

Yeah, the potential for too much clutter is why I'd want the option to control whether the lines are displayed.

I also agree about having the option of seeing the means and contours. Definitely doable.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] scatterplots with time
parts:
If you want to be really slick then you can add lines whose opacity varies with the number
of points in the plot (many points the lines go away, few points they become visible). These
are the kinds of applications where you can go crazy with the eye candy.
